statement: In the norms above, shell integration and designated local subtractions give an exact identity EZu(K; ψ + ζ) = Y b∈BLu (1 + ab)ZLu(K′ ; ψ), Cov(ζ) = Γu. (2.14) The map is complex analytic in small activity inputs, uniformly in finite volume, and its nonlinear remainder is bounded by CL,Aε2 when the activity norm and separately measured singleton coefficients are at most ε. It preserves the common-shift period and all symmetries respected by the localizations. The linear map restricted to large supports has arbitrarily small operator norm, relative to the input activity norm, after choosing A sufficiently large at fixed L. For small field-even neutral bulk inputs, subtraction of the constant and quadratic gradient term gives CL−3 before counting fine placements. Subtracting only the constant gives CL−2 for even inputs and CL−1 without evenness. There are respectively O(L2), O(L), and O(1) placements at a bulk block, a specified wall, and a fixed mark. At α2 = 8π, the fundamental charge has gain O(L−2); for field-even bulk inputs, subtraction of its constant-background cosine coefficient gives an additional L−1. Higher charges have summable stronger gains.
